title: Isolation of Mesenchymal Stem Cells from Human Alveolar Periosteum and Effects of Vitamin D on Osteogenic Activity of Periosteum-derived Cells
protocol: Harvest periosteal tissues from patients during dental surgery.
Store harvested periosteal tissue slices in DPBS with penicillin and streptomycin.
Transfer the tissues to the laboratory within 24 hours.
Mince alveolar periosteal tissue fragments using scalpels.
Maintain minced samples in passage 0 medium in an incubator at 37 °C with humidified air (5% carbon dioxide).
Change the medium after 3 days and twice per week thereafter.
Release adherent cells with trypsin when they reach subconfluence (80%).
Terminate the reaction with medium after trypsin treatment.
Plate released cells in fresh passage 1 medium.
Culture the isolated PDCs in α-MEM supplemented with 10% FBS, 100 U/mL of penicillin, and 100 mg/mL of streptomycin in an incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2).
Observe cell growth daily.
Replace the growth medium twice per week.
Harvest 1 × 10^6 cells through trypsin digestion by adding 200 µL of 0.25% trypsin.
Use 4.5 mL of culture medium containing FBS to terminate the reaction and collect the cells through centrifugation (1500 rpm, 5 min, 22 °C).
Wash the cell pellets three times using 1x DPBS.
Resuspend the cells in 200 µL 1x permeabilization buffer.
Count the cells with a hemocytometer.
Examine the expressed surface markers of PDCs through flow cytometry.
Add monoclonal antibodies (MAb) against CD19, CD34, CD44, CD45, CD73, CD90, CD146, STRO-1, and HLA-DR to the samples.
Culture the samples in the dark at 4 °C for 30 min.
Wash the cells with 1x DPBS three times.
Culture periosteal cells in six-well plates for osteogenic, adipogenic, and chondrogenic differentiation.
For osteogenic differentiation, culture cells in α-MEM at a density of 5000 cells per well on six-well plates.
When the cells reach 80% confluence, switch to media containing α-MEM, 5% FBS, β-glycerophosphate (10 mM), dexamethasone (10−7 M), and ascorbic acid (100 uM).
Culture negative control in media consisting of α-MEM and 5% FBS.
Change the differentiation media twice per week.
After 4 weeks, assess osteogenic potential by staining cells using a von Kossa assay.
Fix cells with 10% formalin.
Within 30 min after fixing, add 5% silver nitrate and treat under UV light for 1 hour at room temperature.
Add 5% Na2SO4 four times, allowing 3 minutes for each addition.
Finally, wash the cells twice with distilled water.
Culture cells at a density of 5000 cells per well on six-well culture plates containing α-MEM.

Culture the cells in media containing α-MEM, 5% FBS, 0.5 mM 3-isobutyl-1-methylxanthine (100 mg/mL), 1% penicillin, 10−6 M dexamethasone (1 mM), insulin (5 mg/mL), and indomethacin (60 mM) when the cells reach 80% confluence.
Culture the negative control in media consisting of α-MEM and 5% FBS.
Fix the cells with 10% formalin for 30 min.
Stain the cells with 0.5% oil red O at room temperature for 10 min.
Wash the cells three times with 60% isopropanol for 3 min each time.
Wash the cells with distilled water.
Culture cells on six-well culture plates with each well containing 5000 cells.

Add a differentiation medium containing α-MEM, 0.1 mM dexamethasone, sodium pyruvate (100 µg/mL), insulin-transferrin-selenium-A (ITS), transforming growth factor-β (10 ng/mL), and ascorbic acid (100 µM).
Culture the negative control in media consisting of α-MEM and 5% FBS.
After 4–5 weeks, use Alcian blue staining to highlight acidic polysaccharides in the cartilage cells.
Add 10% formalin for fixing.
Within 30 min, add 3% acetic acid and allow 2 min for the reaction.
Wash with distilled water three times.
Add 1% Alcian blue 8GX and incubate for 30 min.
Wash with distilled water.
Add 3% acetic acid and wash for 3 min.
Wash with distilled water to finish.
Add 2 mL of the medium to an incubator (37 °C) in each well.
Change the medium twice every week.
Isolate total RNA on ice by using a commercial reagent.
Add 1 mL of isolation reagent to each well.
Add 200 µL of bromochloropropane and leave for 10 min to generate layered RNA, then centrifuge at 10,000 rpm for 15 min at 4 °C.
After centrifugation, add 500 µL of 2-propanol to 500 µL of the supernatant containing RNA.
Centrifuge at 12,000 rpm for 15 min at 4 °C after precipitating RNA on ice and allowing a reaction for 15 minutes.
Remove the supernatant by using 1 mL of 75% alcohol for washing and centrifuge at 7,500 rpm for 8 min in 4 °C.
Use a vacuum concentrator to produce RNA from the bottom of the liquid and recover with water.
Reverse transcribe RNA (1 μg) using avian myeloblastosis virus reverse transcriptase.
Set polymerase chain reaction (PCR) to run at 25 °C for 10 min followed by 50 °C for 60 min, then 85 °C for 5 min before maintaining at 4 °C.
Synthesize first-strand complementary DNA (cDNA).
Perform quantitative PCR (qPCR) using 5 μL of 1:10 diluted cDNA.
Conduct quantitative RT-PCR (qRT-PCR) using primers for ALP, BSP, OCN, CBFA1, and collagen-1.
Set the thermal cycler at 50 °C for 2 min followed by 95 °C for 10 min.
Run 40 cycles each at 95 °C for 15 s followed by 60 °C for 60 s.
Normalize the cycle threshold values for ALP, BSP, CBFA1, collagen-1, and OCN to that of the housekeeping gene GAPDH.
Assess the ALP enzyme activity of the cells using a previously described technique.
Convert p-nitrophenyl phosphate to p-nitrophenol by ALP.
Normalize the total p-nitrophenol formed based on the total protein as determined by the Bradford assay.

Compare ALP activities of control (α-MEM, 5% FBS), Vitamin C (α-MEM, 5% FBS, 10 mM β-glycerophosphate, 10−7 M dexamethasone + 100 μM Vitamin C), 1,25-(OH)2D3 (α-MEM, 5% FBS, 10 mM β-glycerophosphate, and 10−7 M dexamethasone + 10−8 M 1,25-(OH)2D3), and Vitamin C + 1,25-(OH)2D3 (α-MEM, 5% FBS, 10 mM β-glycerophosphate, 10−7 M dexamethasone + 100 μM Vitamin C + 1,25-(OH)2D3) groups after 1, 2, 3, and 4 weeks of culture.
Scrape cells from the 6-well plates.
Add 50 µL of lysis buffer to the scraped cells.
Place the mixture on ice for 30 min to destroy cells and free proteins.
Centrifuge at 13000 rpm at 4 °C for 15 min.
Extract the supernatant after centrifugation.
Store the extracted supernatant for future use.
